My beans are intercropped, so I will not waste money on chemical fertilizer — beans feed themselves from the soil, and whatever little nutrients I can spare I save for when I plant cereal. I will put some manure from my animals on the plot before the rains, that is what my father did and the soil here needs it. The real trouble with cowpea is the insects — the pods get eaten if you do not spray, so I will buy pesticide for one or two sprayings when flowering comes. I will use my own seeds from last harvest, and my wife and children will help me weed; for harvest I may call two young men for a few days.
